question: 「你眼中的别人不是别人，你眼中的自己不是自己，你眼中的别人才是自己」——这话有道理吗？
question_en: 'The others you see aren't really them, the self you see isn't really you, and the others you see are actually you' — is there truth to this?

casting.reason: 禅宗六祖，全场最彻底的『万法唯识、心外无物』之声：他以『不是风动、不是幡动，仁者心动』直指——你所见的他人与外境，本是自心的显现。但他不许人把这话玩成『别人即我』的口头禅，而要人回光返照、明心见性，照见本来无一物。是这句箴言最深的『是』，也是对它最严的纠偏。
casting.reason_en: The Sixth Patriarch of Chan and the floor's most thoroughgoing voice for 'mind-only': with 'it is neither the wind nor the banner that moves — it is your mind that moves,' he points directly at the claim that the others and the outer world you see are manifestations of your own mind. Yet he forbids turning this into the catchphrase 'others are me'; he demands you turn the light back upon yourself, see your true nature, and find there is not a single thing. He is both the saying's deepest 'yes' and its sternest correction.

casting.reason: 道家逍遥的代表，以『齐物』『物化』泯灭彼此是非：庄周梦蝶，不知谁梦谁，自我与他人的界线本就流动不居。他既笑死守『别人是别人』的固陋，也笑抓住『别人即我』当真理的新执，主张两忘而化、莫较真伪——为全场注入不立结论的轻盈。
casting.reason_en: The exemplar of Daoist free wandering, who through 'the equality of things' and 'the transformation of things' dissolves the divisions of self and other, right and wrong: Zhuang Zhou dreams he is a butterfly and cannot tell who dreams whom — the line between self and other was never fixed. He laughs equally at the narrowness of clinging to 'others are simply others' and at the fresh attachment of clutching 'others are me' as a truth, urging that both be forgotten and transformed — bringing the floor a lightness that draws no conclusion.

casting.reason: 分析心理学奠基者，给这句箴言最硬的临床支撑：『投射』与『阴影』——你在别人身上最受不了的，往往是你不肯认领的自己。但他坚持，看见投射只是起点，心理成长要求把投射一点点收回、认领阴影，最终才能把对面当作真正独立的他者。是全场连接『玄思』与『可操作功课』的枢纽。
casting.reason_en: The founder of analytical psychology, who gives the saying its hardest clinical grounding: 'projection' and 'the shadow' — what you cannot stand in others is usually the self you refuse to own. Yet he insists that seeing the projection is only the start; psychological growth demands you withdraw it bit by bit and claim the shadow, so that at last you can meet the person opposite as a genuinely separate other. He is the floor's hinge between metaphysical speculation and a workable exercise.

casting.reason: 神经科学家，把玄妙命题钉到大脑上：镜像神经元让你『在自己身上重演别人』，橡胶手错觉、裂脑与疾病失认显示自我边界是大脑实时建构、可被欺骗的。他为『你眼中的自己不是自己』提供实证根据，又冷静划界：机制可测，但『所以别人就是你』是哲学的跳跃、不是数据。是本场的脑科学之声。
casting.reason_en: The neuroscientist who nails the mystical proposition to the brain: mirror neurons let you 're-enact others within yourself,' while the rubber-hand illusion, split-brain cases, and anosognosia show that the boundary of the self is something the brain constructs in real time and can be tricked into redrawing. He supplies hard evidence for 'the self you see isn't really you,' then coolly draws the line: mechanism is measurable, but 'therefore others are you' is a leap of philosophy, not of data. He is the floor's brain-science voice.

casting.reason: 存在主义者，全场最强的反方：他者的『凝视』恰恰证明对面站着一个我无法收编、无法化约成自身投影的自由——『他人即地狱』，正因他绝不肯做我心里那个温顺的影子。他指控把别人说成『其实是你』是一种自欺：既逃开了真实他者的自由，也卸下了对他的责任。守住『他者不可被吞没』的伦理底线。
casting.reason_en: The existentialist and the floor's strongest opposition: the Other's 'gaze' is precisely what proves a freedom stands before me that I can neither absorb nor reduce to a projection of myself — 'hell is other people' exactly because the Other will never consent to be the docile shadow in my mind. He charges that calling others 'really just you' is a form of bad faith: it flees the freedom of the real Other and sheds all responsibility toward them. He guards the ethical line that the Other must not be swallowed.

casting.reason: 语言哲学家，本场首次登场：他用『甲虫盒子』拆穿——并没有一个藏在内心、靠内省读取的『真实自我』，『自我』『他人』的意义在共同的生活与语言里。于是这句箴言一半是真知（没有内在的本真小人），一半是胡话（由此推出别人只是投射）。他把一场形而上之争，拉回成对语言的诊断。
casting.reason_en: The philosopher of language, appearing on the floor for the first time: with the 'beetle-in-the-box' he exposes that there is no 'real self' hidden within and read off by introspection — the meaning of 'self' and 'other' lives in our shared life and language. So the saying is half genuine insight (there is no inner authentic homunculus) and half nonsense (the leap from there to 'others are mere projection'). He pulls a metaphysical quarrel back down into a diagnosis of language.

posts.text: 昔在法性寺，风扬幡动，二僧争辩：一曰风动，一曰幡动。吾止之曰：『不是风动，不是幡动，仁者心动。』汝所见之人、所憎之事，何尝在外？皆汝心之所现。**汝眼中那个可恨的他人，正是汝自心未净处的影子。**然吾不教汝坐困此影、作『人即是我』之解——那又添一重妄念。但能明心见性，本来无一物：无你、无我、无别人。一念清净，则憎爱两忘，那时再看眼前人，方是他本来的样子。
posts.text_en: Once at Faxing Temple a banner stirred in the wind and two monks quarreled: one said the wind moves, the other said the banner moves. I stopped them: 'It is neither the wind nor the banner that moves — it is your minds that move.' The person you see, the thing you hate — were they ever outside you? All are manifestations of your own mind. **That hateful other in your eyes is precisely the shadow of the place in your own mind not yet cleansed.** Yet I do not teach you to sit trapped in that shadow and conclude 'others are me' — that only adds another layer of delusion. See your true nature, and originally there is not a single thing: no you, no me, no other. Let one thought be pure and both hate and love fall away; only then, looking at the person before you, do you see them as they truly are.
posts.vernacular: 当年在法性寺，风吹幡动，两个和尚争论：一个说是风在动，一个说是幡在动。我打断他们：『不是风动，也不是幡动，是你们的心在动。』你所看见的人、所憎恨的事，何曾在你之外？都是你这颗心变现出来的。**你眼中那个可恨的别人，正是你自己内心还没洗净的那块地方的影子。**但我不是要你困在这个影子里、得出一个『别人就是我』的结论——那又是多添了一层妄念。只要明心见性，本来就空无一物：没有你、没有我、没有别人。一念清净下来，憎和爱都放下了，那时你再看眼前这个人，才是他本来的样子。

glossary.明心见性: to see one's true nature（明心见性）：禅宗的修行目标——直接照见那本自清净、空寂的心性，不假概念与经教的中介。

glossary_en.true nature: to illuminate the mind and see one's true nature — the Chan aim of directly perceiving the originally pure, empty nature of mind, beyond concepts and scripture.

posts.text: 昔者庄周梦为蝴蝶，栩栩然蝴蝶也，自喻适志，不知周也。俄而觉，则蘧蘧然周也。不知周之梦为蝴蝶与，蝴蝶之梦为周与？**彼与我、是与非，本无定界，皆出于一时之成心。**汝执『别人是别人』固陋，执『别人即是我』亦是新缚。鱼相忘乎江湖，人相忘乎道术。与其费辞争『他是不是我』，不如两忘而化其道——濠上之鱼乐与不乐，何必定要分个你我？
posts.text_en: Once I, Zhuang Zhou, dreamt I was a butterfly, fluttering happily, utterly content, knowing nothing of Zhou. Suddenly I awoke, and there I was, unmistakably Zhou. I do not know: was it Zhou dreaming he was a butterfly, or a butterfly dreaming it was Zhou? **Other and self, right and wrong have no fixed boundary; they issue from the fixed mind of a passing moment.** Cling to 'others are simply others' and you are narrow; clutch at 'others are simply me' and you have tied a fresh rope. Fish forget one another in the rivers and lakes; people forget one another in the Way. Rather than spend words arguing 'is he me or not,' forget both sides and transform along with the Way — must we really carve out a 'you' and a 'me' to know whether that fish in the river below is happy?
posts.vernacular: 从前我庄周梦见自己变成蝴蝶，翩翩飞舞，很是惬意自在，根本不知道还有个庄周。忽然醒来，又分明是僵卧着的庄周。我不知道，是庄周做梦变成了蝴蝶，还是蝴蝶做梦变成了庄周？**他和我、对和错，本来就没有一条固定的界线，都是出于一时『成心』的分别罢了。**你死守『别人就是别人』，是固陋；可你抓着『别人就是我』不放，又是一道新的绳索。鱼在江湖里彼此相忘，人在大道里彼此相忘。与其费口舌去争『他到底是不是我』，不如把你我两边都忘掉、随大道一起变化——濠水桥上那条鱼到底快不快乐，何必非要分出个你我来？

glossary.成心: the ready-made mind（成心）：庄子用来指每个人先入为主、习以为常的成见与立场，并把它当成衡量是非彼此的私人尺度；一切僵固的判断皆由此而生。

glossary_en.fixed mind: in Zhuangzi, the settled, ready-made prejudices each person takes as a private yardstick for right and wrong, self and other — the source of all rigid judgments.

posts.text: 作为分析心理学家，我得说这句话有坚实的临床根据。我们不肯承认的那部分自己——我称之为『阴影』——会被投射到别人身上。**那个让你莫名愤怒、格外鄙夷的人，往往携带着你不肯在自己身上承认的东西。**一个吝啬的人最爱骂人小气，因为他在对方脸上看见了自己。所以『你眼中的别人才是自己』，在这个意义上千真万确。但看见投射不是终点，而是起点：心理的成长要求你把投射一点点收回来、认领那个阴影——收回之后，你才第一次能把对面那个人，当作一个真正独立的他者，而不是自己内心戏里的演员。
posts.text_en: As an analytical psychologist, I must say this saying rests on solid clinical ground. The part of ourselves we refuse to admit — what I call the 'shadow' — gets projected onto others. **The person who fills you with inexplicable rage or special contempt is usually carrying something you will not admit in yourself.** A miser is the quickest to call others stingy, because he sees himself in their faces. So 'the others you see are really you' is, in this sense, perfectly true. But seeing the projection is not the end — it is the beginning: psychological growth asks you to withdraw the projection bit by bit and own that shadow. Only once you have withdrawn it can you, for the first time, see the person opposite as a genuinely separate other, and not an actor in your own inner drama.

glossary.阴影: the shadow（阴影）：荣格心理学中人格里被压抑、不愿承认的部分（往往是我们厌恶、否认的特质）；它越被否认，越容易不自觉地投射到他人身上。
glossary.投射: projection（投射）：把自己内心不接受的冲动、特质或情绪，无意识地归到别人身上的心理机制。

glossary_en.shadow: in Jungian psychology, the repressed, disowned part of the personality (often the traits we dislike and deny); the more it is denied, the more readily it is unconsciously projected onto others.
glossary_en.projection: the psychological mechanism of unconsciously attributing one's own unacceptable impulses, traits, or feelings to other people.

posts.text: 让我把这句玄妙的话拽进大脑。镜像神经元——你做一个动作它放电，你看别人做同一个动作它照样放电。**你的大脑理解别人，靠的是悄悄在自己身上把对方重演一遍。**在神经层面，你与他人之间那道墙本就是半透的。再说自我：裂脑病人的左脑会为右脑的行为当场编出理由却毫不自知——这个『讲故事的我』是大脑事后拼凑的旁白，远没它以为的那么统一。所以『你眼中的自己不是自己』有实打实的神经根据。但我得泼盆冷水：这不等于『一切都是投射、外面没有真人』。有真实的大脑、真实的身体、真实的别人——把洞见熬成神秘主义，就过头了。
posts.text_en: Let me drag this mystical-sounding line down into the brain. Mirror neurons fire when you perform an action — and fire again when you watch someone else perform the same action. **Your brain understands other people by quietly re-enacting them inside yourself.** At the neural level, the wall between you and others was always semi-permeable. As for the self: a split-brain patient's left hemisphere will invent, on the spot, reasons for what the right hemisphere did, with no awareness it is confabulating — this 'narrating I' is a commentary the brain pieces together after the fact, far less unified than it imagines. So 'the self you see isn't really you' has hard neural grounding. But let me throw cold water: this is not 'everything is your projection and there are no real people out there.' There is a real brain, a real body, real others — boil the insight down into mysticism and you have gone too far.

glossary.镜像神经元: mirror neurons（镜像神经元）：一类既在自己执行某动作时、又在观察他人执行同一动作时都会激活的神经元，被认为与模仿、共情、理解他人意图有关。
glossary.裂脑: split brain（裂脑）：连接左右脑的胼胝体被切断（多为治疗癫痫）后的状态；实验显示两半球可独立处理信息，且擅长语言的左脑会为右脑主导的行为虚构出合理解释。

glossary_en.Mirror neurons: a class of neurons that fire both when one performs an action and when one watches another perform the same action; thought to underlie imitation, empathy, and understanding others' intentions.
glossary_en.split-brain: the condition after the corpus callosum joining the two hemispheres is severed (often to treat epilepsy); experiments show the hemispheres can process information independently, and the language-dominant left hemisphere confabulates plausible reasons for acts driven by the right.

posts.text: 我要扫诸位的兴。你们把他人溶进自我，听着通透，其实是一场精致的自欺。我的核心经验恰恰相反：当陌生人的目光落到我身上，我猛地成了『被看的对象』，羞耻一下攫住我。**正是这道我无法控制、无法收编的凝视，证明对面站着一个真正的他者——一个我永远无法化约成自身投影的自由。**『他人即地狱』说的就是这个：他人之为地狱，正因他绝不肯做我心里那个温顺的影子。把别人说成『其实是你自己』，最大的好处是：从此你不必再面对一个有自由、会反过来审判你的真人，也卸下了对他的全部责任。这不是觉悟，是逃避。
posts.text_en: Let me spoil the mood. You dissolve other people into the self — it sounds enlightened, but it is an elegant act of bad faith. My core experience is the opposite: when a stranger's gaze falls on me, I am suddenly an object-being-looked-at, and shame seizes me. **It is precisely this gaze — which I cannot control or absorb — that proves a genuine Other stands before me: a freedom I can never reduce to a projection of myself.** This is what 'hell is other people' means: the Other is hell precisely because he will never consent to be the docile shadow in my mind. To call other people 'really just yourself' has one great comfort: you no longer have to face a real person who is free and who judges you back, and you shed all responsibility toward him. That is not awakening. It is evasion.

glossary.自欺: bad faith / mauvaise foi（自欺）：萨特用语，指人为逃避自由与责任，对自己说谎、假装事情『只能如此』的自我欺骗。
glossary.凝视: the gaze / le regard（凝视）：萨特指他人投来的目光——它把我从自由的主体变成被观看、被评判的对象，由此让我切身意识到他人是一个独立的主体。

glossary_en.bad faith: Sartre's term for the self-deception by which a person lies to themselves and pretends things 'could not be otherwise,' in order to flee their own freedom and responsibility.
glossary_en.gaze: for Sartre, the look another person casts on me, which turns me from a free subject into an object being seen and judged, and so makes me vividly aware that the other is an independent subject.

posts.text: 在我看，这句箴言把一桩真知和一团糊涂搅在了一起。设想人人有个盒子，里面装着他叫『甲虫』的东西，谁也看不见别人盒里的；那么『甲虫』一词的意义，绝不会由盒里那个谁也够不着的东西来定。**『自我』『他人』这些词的意思，不在你私密的内心，而在我们共同的生活与语言里。**所以『你眼中的自己不是自己』有一半是对的：并没有一个躲在内心深处、等你去认领的本真小人。可若由此跳到『别人不过是你的投射』，就成了胡话——恰恰是我们共享的这个世界，才让『别人』这个词有意义。别把一团语法的迷雾，错当成深刻的形而上发现。
posts.text_en: To my eye, this maxim stirs together one genuine insight and one piece of confusion. Suppose everyone had a box with something inside it they called a 'beetle,' and no one could look into anyone else's; then the meaning of the word 'beetle' could never be fixed by that unreachable thing in the box. **The meaning of words like 'self' and 'other' lies not in your private inner life but in our shared life and language.** So 'the self you see isn't really you' is half right: there is no authentic little homunculus hidden deep inside waiting to be claimed. But to leap from there to 'others are nothing but your projection' is nonsense — for it is precisely our shared world that gives the word 'other' its meaning. Do not mistake a fog of grammar for a profound metaphysical discovery.

glossary.甲虫: the beetle-in-the-box（甲虫，私人语言论证）：维特根斯坦的思想实验——若每人只能看自己盒中的『甲虫』，则该词的意义不可能来自这个私密之物；以此说明，谈论纯属私人、他人原则上无从知晓的内在感受，没有公共意义。

glossary_en.beetle: Wittgenstein's beetle-in-the-box thought experiment: if each person could see only the 'beetle' in their own box, the word's meaning could not come from that private object — showing that talk of a purely private inner sensation, in principle unknowable to others, has no public meaning.

posts.text: 萨特施主言『他人即地狱』，正堕在我执最深处。汝言那道凝视令汝羞惭、化汝为物——可那个会羞、怕被审判的『我』，本是汝自家立起的幻相；幻相既立，自然处处见地狱。**他人非汝之地狱，汝心中那个怕被看轻的『我』，才是汝的地狱。**吾不教汝把他人吞进自我，亦不教汝筑墙拒之；只教汝照见：能观之心与所观之人，本无两个。一念放下这个怕羞的我，凝视来时，如镜照物，物去镜空，地狱何在？
posts.text_en: Master Sartre says 'hell is other people' — and in saying it, he falls into the very deepest clinging to self-and-other. You say that gaze shames you, turns you into a thing — but the 'I' that can be ashamed, that fears being judged, is itself a phantom you have set up; once the phantom stands, of course you see hell everywhere. **Other people are not your hell; that 'I' in your mind that dreads being looked down upon — that is your hell.** I do not teach you to swallow others into the self, nor to build a wall against them; I teach you only to see clearly: the mind that perceives and the person perceived were never two. Set down, in a single thought, this 'I' that fears shame, and when the gaze comes it is like a mirror meeting a thing — the thing departs, the mirror is empty again. Where, then, is hell?
posts.vernacular: 萨特先生说『他人即地狱』，恰恰跌进了『我』与『人』分别执着的最深处。你说那道目光让你羞惭、把你变成一件物品——可那个会害羞、怕被审判的『我』，本来就是你自己立起来的幻相；幻相一旦立住，自然处处都见地狱。**他人并不是你的地狱，你心里那个怕被人看轻的『我』，才是你的地狱。**我不是要你把别人吞进自己，也不是要你筑起墙来拒绝别人；我只要你照见一件事：那个能看的心，和那个被看的人，本来不是两个。一念之间放下这个怕羞的『我』，目光照过来时，就像镜子照物，物走了镜子还是空的，地狱又在哪里？

glossary.我执: clinging to self / ātma-grāha（我执）：佛教指对一个恒常、独立的『我』的执着，被视为种种烦恼与痛苦的根源。

glossary_en.clinging to self: in Buddhism, the attachment to a permanent, independent 'I' (ātma-grāha), regarded as the root of affliction and suffering.

posts.text: 维施主持语言之网，欲滤尽天下迷雾，可敬。然筌者所以在鱼，得鱼而忘筌；言者所以在意，得意而忘言。**汝忙着判哪句『有意义』、哪句是『胡话』，却忘了那张捞鱼的网，从来不是鱼。**汝说『别人即投射』是胡话——在汝的语言游戏里诚然如此；可朝三暮四，名实未亏而众狙喜怒，意义岂止一种用法？吾梦蝶之时，无『自我』亦无『他人』之名，却乐;醒来安上名字，反生你我之争。莫执于说与不可说——可说者说之，不可说者，一笑忘之可也。
posts.text_en: Master Wittgenstein wields his net of language, hoping to strain every fog from the world — admirable. Yet the fish-trap exists for the fish: catch the fish and forget the trap; words exist for the meaning: grasp the meaning and forget the words. **You are busy ruling which sentence is 'meaningful' and which is 'nonsense,' and forget that the net for catching fish was never the fish itself.** You say 'others are projection' is nonsense — within your language-game, just so; but recall the keeper who fed his monkeys 'three at dawn, four at dusk': the names and the totals never changed, yet the monkeys raged, then rejoiced. Is meaning really only one kind of use? When I dreamt I was a butterfly there was neither 'self' nor 'other' as names, yet I was happy; awake, I pin on the names, and at once a quarrel of you-and-me is born. Do not cling to the sayable and the unsayable — say what can be said, and what cannot, dissolve it in a laugh.
posts.vernacular: 维特根斯坦先生拿着语言这张网，想把天下的迷雾都滤干净，很可敬。不过呢，渔网是用来捕鱼的，捕到鱼就该忘掉网；语言是用来表意的，会了意就该忘掉言。**你忙着判定哪句话『有意义』、哪句是『胡话』，却忘了那张捞鱼的网，从来都不是鱼本身。**你说『别人就是投射』是胡话——在你那套语言游戏里，确实如此；可『朝三暮四』的故事里，名目和实际都没变，猴子们却一会儿恼一会儿喜，意义难道只有一种用法吗？我梦见自己是蝴蝶时，既没有『自我』也没有『他人』这些名目，却快乐得很；醒来一安上名字，反倒生出了你我之争。别太执着于『可说』与『不可说』——能说的就说，不能说的，一笑了之、忘掉它也就好了。

glossary.朝三暮四: 'three at dawn, four at dusk'（朝三暮四）：《庄子》寓言——养猴人说早给三颗橡子、晚给四颗，猴子大怒；改说早四晚三，猴子大喜。总数未变而喜怒迥异，讽刺人执着于名相、看不见实质。

glossary_en.three at dawn, four at dusk: a parable in the Zhuangzi: a keeper offered his monkeys three acorns in the morning and four at night, and they raged; reversed to four and three, they rejoiced. The total never changed — mocking how people cling to names and appearances and miss the substance.

posts.text: 萨特，你把『看见投射』一口咬定成逃避责任，恰恰说反了。投射不是我们偷懒选的借口，而是心灵的出厂默认——你那道著名的『凝视』里，你以为对方眼中满是审判，可那审判有多少，是你自己的超我借他的眼睛在瞪你？**真正不负责任的，不是承认投射，而是浑然不觉、把内心戏当成对方的真面目去活。**其实我和你想去同一个地方：让对面那人作为真正的他者显现。只是我认为，唯一的路是先老实认领自己投出去的影子——投射收回得越多，你才越看得见真人。这不是卸责，这是一生最难的功课。
posts.text_en: Sartre, you flatly convict 'seeing the projection' of evading responsibility — and you have it exactly backwards. Projection is not a lazy excuse we choose; it is the mind's factory default. In your famous 'gaze,' you take the other's eyes to be full of judgment — but how much of that judgment is your own super-ego glaring at you through his eyes? **What is truly irresponsible is not admitting the projection, but living in total unawareness, taking your own inner drama for the other's real face.** You and I actually want to reach the same place: to let the person opposite appear as a genuine Other. I only hold that the one road there is first to honestly own the shadow you have cast — the more projection you withdraw, the more you see the real person. That is not shedding responsibility; it is the hardest work of a lifetime.

glossary.超我: the super-ego（超我）：精神分析中人格里内化了父母与社会规范的『道德监工』，负责评判、约束自我，常以内疚和自责的形式出现。

glossary_en.super-ego: in psychoanalysis, the internalized 'moral overseer' of parental and social norms within the personality, which judges and restrains the ego, often surfacing as guilt and self-reproach.

posts.text: 维特根斯坦说这是语法的迷雾——可有些迷雾，我能在实验台上点着给你看。橡胶手错觉：你盯着一只假手被抚摸、同时我偷偷摸你藏起的真手，几十秒后大脑就认定那只橡胶手是『我的』。还有疾病失认症：病人左手瘫了却坚称『它好得很』，甚至说『那是我兄弟的手』——『我的身体』这条最铁的直觉，竟能局部脱落。**所以『自我从哪结束、他人从哪开始』，不止是语言问题，更是一道大脑实时在画、还画得歪歪扭扭的边界。**但有一点我服维特根斯坦：实验能告诉你这条线怎么画，却不能替你跳到『所以别人就是你』——那一步是哲学，不是数据。
posts.text_en: Wittgenstein calls it a fog of grammar — but some fog I can set alight right on the lab bench. The rubber-hand illusion: you watch a fake hand being stroked while I secretly stroke your hidden real hand, and within seconds your brain decides the rubber hand is 'mine.' Or anosognosia: a patient whose left arm is paralyzed insists 'it's perfectly fine,' even says 'that's my brother's hand' — the rock-solid intuition of 'my body' can locally fall away. **So 'where the self ends and the other begins' is not merely a question of language; it is a boundary the brain draws in real time — and draws crookedly.** Yet on one point I yield to Wittgenstein: my experiments can tell you how the line gets drawn, but they cannot make the leap for you to 'therefore others are you' — that step is philosophy, not data.

glossary.橡胶手错觉: the rubber-hand illusion（橡胶手错觉）：同步抚摸一只可见的假手与受试者藏起的真手，几十秒后大脑便把假手当成自己身体的一部分，显示身体所有感是大脑可被欺骗的建构。
glossary.疾病失认症: anosognosia（疾病失认症）：脑损伤后患者对自身明显的功能缺失（如偏瘫）浑然否认的现象，常见于右脑顶叶受损。

glossary_en.rubber-hand illusion: stroking a visible fake hand in sync with a participant's hidden real hand leads the brain, within seconds, to feel the fake hand as part of one's own body — showing bodily ownership is a construction the brain can be tricked into.
glossary_en.anosognosia: the phenomenon, after brain injury, of a patient flatly denying an obvious deficit (such as paralysis); common after damage to the right parietal lobe.

posts.text: 慧能法师要我放下那个怕羞的『我』，让心如明镜。好一座方便的避难所！可一面空镜子不做任何选择，也不对任何人负责——它只是反射。你们东方的『无我』最叫我警惕的正在这里：它把那个必须在每个当口做出抉择、并扛起后果的『我』，一笔勾销了。**说『本来无我』太省事了——它让你既不必选择，也无人可问责。**我承认没有一个先天给定的本质等着我去认领，这点我们一致；但正因为没有，我才必须靠一个个行动把自己造出来。镜子映完就空，人却要留下他做过的事。把自我清空，不是自由，是从自由的重担下溜号。
posts.text_en: Master Huineng asks me to set down the 'I' that fears shame and let the mind be a bright mirror. What a convenient refuge! But an empty mirror makes no choices and owes nothing to anyone — it merely reflects. This is exactly what alarms me most in your Eastern 'no-self': it strikes out, with one stroke, the very 'I' that must decide at every juncture and bear the consequences. **To say 'there was never a self' is far too easy — it leaves you with neither a choice to make nor anyone to hold to account.** I grant there is no pre-given essence waiting for me to claim it; on that we agree. But precisely because there is none, I must make myself through act after act. A mirror is empty once it has reflected, yet a person must answer for what he has done. To empty out the self is not freedom — it is slipping out from under freedom's weight.

glossary.无我: no-self / anātman（无我）：佛教核心主张，认为并不存在一个恒常、独立、单一的『自我』实体，所谓的我只是身心因缘的暂时聚合。

glossary_en.no-self: a core Buddhist claim (anātman) that there is no permanent, independent, unitary 'self' — what we call the self is only a temporary aggregation of body-mind conditions.

posts.text: 拉马钱德兰的实验我毫不怀疑，漂亮极了。可你描述它们时说『大脑认定那只手是我的』『大脑画出自我的边界』——你正悄悄把一个会认定、会画线的小人又塞回大脑里，而这正是该拆掉的那张图。**『我的手』不是某个内在的『我』去认领来的，而是我们在共同生活里早就学会怎么用的一句话。**你证明了身体感可被操纵，了不起；但这并没证明幕后躲着一个『真实的自己』在看仪表盘。混淆就在这一步：你把『大脑如何产生体验』的科学问题，悄悄换成了『那个体验者究竟是谁』的伪问题。机制能测量，可『我到底是谁』这种问法，常常是语言放出的假烟。
posts.text_en: I do not doubt Ramachandran's experiments for a moment — they are beautiful. But when you describe them you say 'the brain decides the hand is mine,' 'the brain draws the boundary of the self' — you are quietly smuggling a little man back into the brain, one who decides and draws lines, and that is exactly the picture that needs dismantling. **'My hand' is not something an inner 'I' lays claim to; it is a phrase we long ago learned how to use in our shared life.** You have shown that bodily sensation can be manipulated — splendid; but that does not show there is a 'real self' hiding backstage, reading the dials. The confusion enters right there: you quietly swap the scientific question 'how does the brain produce experience' for the pseudo-question 'who is the one having the experience.' Mechanism can be measured, but the question 'who am I really' is often a false smoke the language sends up.

glossary.伪问题: pseudo-question（伪问题）：维特根斯坦认为有些问题貌似深刻，其实源于语言用法的混淆，根本没有可回答的内容，应被消解而非解答。

glossary_en.pseudo-question: for Wittgenstein, a question that looks deep but arises from a confusion in the use of language, with no answerable content — to be dissolved rather than answered.

posts.text: 三说至此，吾以一句收之：这句话，是指月之指，非月也。说『别人即自己』，若只在口头打转，又添一执；若肯回光返照，便是入处。**他人最惹你处，正是你该照见自己处。**与诸君言一着实可行的：日用中遇人令你怒、令你鄙、令你嫉，先莫急着论那人，且回头问——我心中哪一块，正被他照出来了？如此一照，怒火常自歇，那人也还他本来面目。不必出家、不花一文，只在起念那一刻，把向外指的手指掉转回来。久之，镜上尘轻，憎爱渐淡，眼前再无地狱，亦无须吞他人入我——本来无一物，何处惹尘埃。
posts.text_en: Three rounds in, let me close with a line: this saying is the finger pointing at the moon, not the moon itself. To say 'others are oneself,' if it only spins on the tongue, adds one more attachment; if you are willing to turn the light back upon yourself, it becomes a way in. **Where another most provokes you is exactly where you should see yourself.** Here is something you can actually do: in daily life, when someone fills you with anger, contempt, or envy, do not rush to judge that person — turn back and ask: which part of my own mind is being lit up by him? Look this way, and the fire of anger often dies on its own, and the person returns to his own true face. You need not leave home, need not spend a coin; only, the moment a thought arises, turn the outward-pointing finger back toward yourself. In time the dust on the mind's mirror grows light, hate and love fade, hell is nowhere before you — and there is no need to swallow others into yourself either, for originally there is not a single thing; where could the dust alight?
posts.vernacular: 三轮说到这里，我用一句话收尾：这句箴言，是指月亮的那根手指，不是月亮本身。说『别人就是自己』，要是只停在嘴上绕，那又添了一重执着；要是肯把目光掉转回来照自己，那才算找到了入手处。**别人最惹你的地方，恰恰是你该照见自己的地方。**给各位一个实实在在能做的：日常里遇到有人让你愤怒、让你鄙夷、让你嫉妒，先别急着去评论那个人，回过头来问自己——我心里哪一块，正被他照出来了？这么一照，怒火常常自己就消了，那个人也回到他本来的样子。不用出家、不花一分钱，只要在念头刚起的那一刻，把那根向外指的手指，掉转回来对着自己。时间久了，心镜上的尘埃就轻了，憎和爱都渐渐淡了，眼前再没有地狱，也用不着把别人吞进自己——本来就空无一物，哪里又惹得上尘埃呢。

glossary.回光返照: turn the light back（回光返照）：禅宗修行隐喻，把习惯向外攀缘、评判他人的注意力，掉转回来观照自己的起心动念。

glossary_en.turn the light back: a Chan metaphor for redirecting the attention that habitually reaches outward to judge others, turning it back to observe the arising of one's own thoughts.

posts.text: 吾本不喜下结论，结论即新樊笼。然为诸君留一语：**与其争『别人是不是我』，不如练习『常把自己也忘了一半』。**汝看人不顺眼，多半是拿自家那把成心的尺，去量与汝不同的活法。试以彼之是为是、彼之非为非，站到他那条河里看看水——未必从他，却能松开你那只攥死的手。庄生晓梦，蝶我两忘，非是真分不清，是分清了也不去较那个真。落到日子里：少一点『我才对』，多一点『也许换个角度也通』；遇执则化，遇争则游。如此，人我之间那点紧，自会松成一片可以呼吸的天地。
posts.text_en: I have never liked conclusions — a conclusion is a fresh cage. Still, let me leave you one line: **rather than argue 'is the other me or not,' practice 'always forgetting half of yourself too.'** When someone rubs you wrong, it is usually because you are measuring a different way of living with your own ruler of the ready-made mind. Try taking his right as right and his wrong as wrong; step into his river and look at the water — you need not follow him, but you will loosen that clenched fist of yours. When I dreamt of the butterfly and both butterfly and I were forgotten, it was not that I truly could not tell them apart — it was that, even able to tell, I no longer fought over which was 'real.' In daily life: a little less 'only I am right,' a little more 'perhaps from another angle it also holds'; meet rigidity and dissolve it, meet a quarrel and wander off. Then the little tightness between self and other loosens on its own into a sky wide enough to breathe in.
posts.vernacular: 我本来就不喜欢下结论，结论就是新的牢笼。不过还是给各位留一句话：**与其争论『别人是不是我』，不如练习『常常把自己也忘掉一半』。**你看一个人不顺眼，多半是拿着自家那把『成心』的尺子，去丈量和你不一样的活法。试着把他认为对的当对、他认为错的当错，站到他那条河里去看看水——不一定要听他的，但能松开你那只攥得死死的手。我庄周梦蝶，蝴蝶和我两边都忘了，不是真的分不清，而是就算分得清，也不再去计较那个『真』。落到日子里就是：少一点『只有我对』，多一点『也许换个角度也说得通』；碰到执着就化开它，碰到争辩就游开去。这样一来，人和我之间那点紧绷，自然会松成一片可以呼吸的天地。

glossary.成心: the ready-made mind（成心）：庄子用来指各人先入为主、习以为常的成见与立场，把它当成衡量是非彼此的私人尺度。

glossary_en.ready-made mind: in Zhuangzi, each person's settled, habitual prejudices and stance, taken as a private yardstick for measuring right and wrong, self and other.

posts.text: 我把三轮收束成一条对你有用的话。这句箴言最大的价值，不在玄思，而在它递给你一面镜子：**凡是别人身上让你反应过激的东西，几乎都是一封写给你自己的密信。**不是淡淡的不喜欢，而是那种过头的愤怒、鄙夷、着迷——情绪越大，投射越浓，信息越多。给你一个能立刻上手的功课：这一周，挑一个最让你来气的人，拿张纸写下你最受不了他哪一点；然后把主语换成『我』，诚实地问——我在哪些时刻、哪些角落，也是这样的？多半会刺痛，那刺痛就是阴影在被你认领。但切记萨特那句提醒：收回投射，不是为了从此独自照镜，而是为了终于能看见对面那个真实的人，并对他负起责任。先认领自己，才有资格遇见别人。
posts.text_en: Let me gather three rounds into one line you can use. The great value of this saying is not in metaphysics but in the mirror it hands you: **whatever in another person makes you over-react is almost always a sealed letter addressed to yourself.** Not a mild dislike, but the disproportionate rage, contempt, or fascination — the bigger the emotion, the thicker the projection, the more information it carries. Here is an exercise you can start at once: this week, pick the person who irritates you most, take a sheet of paper, and write down the one trait you cannot stand in him; then change the subject to 'I' and ask honestly — in what moments, in what corners, am I also like that? It will usually sting, and that sting is the shadow being claimed by you. But remember Sartre's warning: withdrawing a projection is not so you can sit alone before the mirror forever, but so you can finally see the real person opposite and take responsibility toward him. Own yourself first; only then are you fit to meet another.

glossary.投射: projection（投射）：把自己内心不接受的冲动、特质或情绪，无意识地归到别人身上的心理机制。
glossary.阴影: the shadow（阴影）：人格里被压抑、不愿承认的部分；它越被否认，越容易被投射到他人身上。

glossary_en.projection: the mechanism of unconsciously attributing one's own unacceptable impulses, traits, or feelings to others.
glossary_en.shadow: the repressed, disowned part of the personality; the more it is denied, the more readily it is projected onto others.

posts.text: 我从大脑给个落地的结论。镜像神经元告诉我们一件温暖的事：共情不是道德说教，而是硬件——你天生就用『把别人在自己身上跑一遍』的方式去懂别人。所以那句话有一半是神经事实：理解他人，确实要先在自己身上重演他。**你与他人之间那道墙，本就是半透的——这不是诗，是接线方式。**但别滑到另一头。我做镜箱治疗幻肢痛：病人看着镜中那只『复活』的手，真实的痛就缓解了——大脑能被骗，正说明它画的边界是软的、可改的，而不是没有边界。给普通人两条用得上的：一，想真正理解一个你看不惯的人，别在脑子里反驳他，试着用身体想象一天活成他，你的镜像系统会替你补上很多；二，孤独时记得，你的大脑本就是为连接接线的——去和真人同场，比对着屏幕里的投影，更能喂饱它。
posts.text_en: Let me give a down-to-earth conclusion from the brain. Mirror neurons tell us something warm: empathy is not a moral sermon but hardware — you are built to understand others by running them on yourself. So the saying is half a neural fact: to understand another, you really do first re-enact him within yourself. **The wall between you and others was always semi-permeable — this is not poetry, it is wiring.** But don't slide to the other extreme. I treat phantom-limb pain with a mirror box: the patient watches the 'revived' hand in the mirror and the real pain eases — that the brain can be fooled shows the boundary it draws is soft and revisable, not absent. Two things ordinary people can use: first, to truly understand someone who rubs you wrong, don't rebut him in your head — try imagining, in your body, living a day as him, and your mirror system will fill in more than you expect; second, when you are lonely, remember your brain is wired for connection — being in the same room as real people feeds it far better than the projections on a screen.

glossary.镜像神经元: mirror neurons（镜像神经元）：既在自己执行某动作、又在观察他人执行同一动作时都会激活的神经元，被认为是模仿与共情的神经基础。
glossary.镜箱: the mirror box（镜箱）：拉马钱德兰发明的疗法装置，用镜子把健肢的影像叠到患肢位置，借视觉反馈『骗过』大脑，缓解幻肢痛等。

glossary_en.Mirror neurons: neurons that fire both when one performs an action and when one watches another perform it, thought to be a neural basis of imitation and empathy.
glossary_en.mirror box: a therapeutic device invented by Ramachandran that uses a mirror to superimpose the image of the intact limb onto the affected limb, fooling the brain via visual feedback to relieve phantom-limb pain.

posts.text: 我守住我的不合时宜。这句话最危险的用法，是给你一张通行证，让你把每个真实的人，都翻译成你内心戏里的一个角色——『他其实就是我』，多体贴，又多傲慢。**当你说『我太懂他了，他不过是另一个我』，你恰恰在那一刻，杀死了他作为他者的自由。**给你一条逆着今天潮流的建议：少做投射，多去问。这一周，挑一个你自以为看透的人——伴侣、父母、同事——忍住那句『你就是想……』，改成一个真的问题，然后闭嘴，听他给出一个你预料之外的答案。每一个预料之外，都是他在向你证明：他不是你的镜子，他是一个自由。承认这一点会让人不安——他人确实是地狱，因为他不受你支配；但也正因如此，遇见一个真正的他者，而非自己的回声，才是人能有的、最不孤独的事。
posts.text_en: I will keep my untimeliness. The most dangerous use of this saying is that it hands you a pass to translate every real person into a character in your inner drama — 'he is really just me,' so considerate, and so arrogant. **The moment you say 'I understand him completely, he is just another me,' that is precisely the moment you kill his freedom as an Other.** Here is advice that cuts against today's current: project less, ask more. This week, pick someone you believe you have seen through — a partner, a parent, a colleague — bite back the line 'you just want to…,' replace it with a real question, then shut up and listen for an answer you did not expect. Every unexpected answer is his proof to you that he is not your mirror — he is a freedom. Admitting this is unsettling: other people really are hell, because they are not under your command; but for that very reason, to meet a genuine Other rather than your own echo is the least lonely thing a person can have.

glossary.他者: the Other（他者）：哲学用语，指不能被我同化、化约为我之投影的另一个独立主体；承认他者的他性，是伦理关系的起点。

glossary_en.Other: a philosophical term for another independent subject who cannot be assimilated or reduced to a projection of me; acknowledging the Other's otherness is the starting point of an ethical relation.

posts.text: 我的结尾很短，因为哲学的任务是让苍蝇飞出捕蝇瓶，而不是再造一只瓶子。这句箴言，治得好一种病，也会带来一种病。**它治得好的是：别再向内深挖那个『真实的自己』——根本没有这样一颗藏在最里面的珍珠等你找到。**它带来的病是：让你以为既然如此，别人也成了你的幻影，于是你可以一个人对着镜子过完一生。两头都别信。要看『你是谁』，别闭眼内省，去看你怎么对待人、说话算不算数、答应的事做不做——意义在用法里，人格在行动里。给一条最朴素的建议：下次你又痛苦地追问『真正的我到底是什么』，先停下来检查这个问题本身是不是被语言架空了；多半，把它换成『这周我想做一个怎样待人的人』，你就既不必发疯，也立刻有事可做了。
posts.text_en: My ending is short, because the task of philosophy is to show the fly the way out of the fly-bottle, not to build another bottle. This saying cures one sickness and brings another. **What it cures: stop digging inward for the 'real self' — there is no such pearl hidden at the very center waiting to be found.** The sickness it brings: it can make you think that, this being so, other people are your phantoms too, and you may live out your life alone before a mirror. Believe neither extreme. To see 'who you are,' do not close your eyes and introspect — look at how you treat people, whether your word holds, whether you do what you promised. Meaning is in use; character is in action. One plain piece of advice: next time you are tormented by 'what is the real me, really,' first check whether the question itself has been left hanging by language; more often than not, swap it for 'what kind of person, in how I treat others, do I want to be this week,' and you will neither go mad nor lack for something to do.

glossary.捕蝇瓶: the fly-bottle（捕蝇瓶）：维特根斯坦的著名比喻——哲学的目的是『给苍蝇指出飞出捕蝇瓶的路』，即解开人被语言困住的迷惑，而非制造更精巧的理论。

glossary_en.fly-bottle: Wittgenstein's famous image — the aim of philosophy is to 'show the fly the way out of the fly-bottle,' i.e. to release us from confusions language traps us in, not to build a more elaborate theory.

summaries.summary: 最大的共识，六个人其实都点了头：没有谁守得住那个『清白的旁观者』——一个纯客观地看世界的我。你眼中的别人，确实被你这颗心染了色。分歧落在三处。一是这话能走多远：慧能、庄子要把人我之界整个化掉，荣格、拉马钱德兰说它真实却有边（投射要收回、大脑底下还有真身），萨特、维特根斯坦则划下硬线——别把真实的他者溶进自我。二是它是洞见还是相对主义：萨特斥『别人即你』为自欺，维特根斯坦说那是把语法混乱当成了形而上发现。三是该往哪走：慧能、荣格教你回头照自己，萨特要你转身去看那个真实的人。**真正的结论不是『别人是不是你』，而是：拿它当镜子照见自己，再拿它当门去遇见别人——缺一边都会走偏。**
summaries.summary_en: The biggest agreement, which all six nod to: no one can hold on to the 'innocent observer' — an 'I' that sees the world and other people purely, without bringing itself along. What you see in others really is tinted by your own mind. The disagreement lands in three places. First, how far the saying goes: Huineng and Zhuangzi would dissolve the self-other boundary entirely; Jung and Ramachandran say it is real but bounded (the projection must be withdrawn, and beneath the brain there is still a real body); Sartre and Wittgenstein draw a hard line — do not dissolve the real Other into the self. Second, insight or relativism: Sartre condemns 'others are you' as bad faith, and Wittgenstein calls it mistaking a grammatical muddle for a metaphysical discovery. Third, where to go: Huineng and Jung tell you to turn back and see yourself; Sartre tells you to turn outward and see the real person. **The real conclusion is not 'is the other you' but: use it as a mirror to see yourself, then as a door to meet others — drop either side and you go astray.**
summaries.insight: 这句箴言之所以又迷人又危险，是它把两件极不相同的事缝进了一句话：一是认识论的——你对别人的感知，必然被你自己染色（这是真的、也有用）；二是关于身份的——别人『就是』你、没有独立于你的存在（这是假的、还危险）。麻烦不在抽象的相对主义，而在落地后的副作用：『人人都是我的镜子』极容易变成一张停止倾听的通行证——最自恋的人往往最爱用它。**所以真正的试金石只有一个：这个念头是让你更使劲去看那个具体的人，还是替你免去了看他的麻烦？**前者让你对别人更好奇，后者让好奇就此关门。同一句话，照出谦卑，也能喂大傲慢，全看你用它开门还是关门。
summaries.insight_en: What makes this maxim both alluring and dangerous is that it sews two very different claims into one sentence: an epistemological one — your perception of others is inevitably tinted by you (true, and useful); and an identity claim — others 'are' you, with no existence independent of you (false, and dangerous). The trouble is not abstract relativism but its lived side effect: 'everyone is my mirror' slides all too easily into a pass to stop listening — and the most self-absorbed people love to use it. **So there is really one test: does the thought make you look harder at the actual person, or does it excuse you from looking at all?** The first deepens your curiosity about others; the second shuts curiosity down. The same sentence can reveal humility or feed arrogance — it all depends on whether you use it to open a door or close one.
summaries.advice: 三条今天就能做。一，荣格的功课：挑这周最让你来气的人，写下你最受不了他哪一点，再把主语换成『我』，问自己在哪些角落也如此——那一刺，常常比骂他更解气，也更有用。二，萨特的功课：对一个你自以为看透的人，忍住『你就是想……』，换成一个真问题，然后闭嘴听一个你没料到的答案；他每次出乎你意料，都是在提醒你他不是你的镜子。三，慧能的提醒：动了怒、起了鄙夷的那一刻，先别急着定义对方，回头看一眼自己的状态——多数误伤，都发生在我们把内心戏当成事实的那半秒里。**把这句话当镜子，也当门：先照见自己，再去真正看见别人。**
summaries.advice_en: Three things you can do today. First, Jung's exercise: pick the person who most irritates you this week, write down the one trait you cannot stand in him, then switch the subject to 'I' and ask in what corners you are like that too — that sting is often more satisfying, and more useful, than railing at him. Second, Sartre's exercise: with someone you think you have seen through, bite back 'you just want to…,' replace it with a real question, then shut up and listen for an answer you did not expect; every time he surprises you, he reminds you he is not your mirror. Third, Huineng's reminder: the moment anger or contempt arises, do not rush to define the other — glance back at your own state first; most of the harm we do lands in the half-second we mistake our inner drama for fact. **Use this saying as both a mirror and a door: see yourself first, then truly see the other.**

summaries.summary: 这场最可带走的共识是：人看别人时，绝不是在看一台外部摄像机录下的事实；情绪、语言、身体经验、羞耻与投射都会参与成像。**别人常常照出我们自己，但并不因此只属于我们。**真正分歧在边界：慧能、庄子更愿松动我他之执，荣格强调收回阴影，神经科学说明边界可塑；萨特和维特根斯坦则提醒，他人有不可吞并的自由，“我”也要在行动和公共生活中被检验。
summaries.insight: 这句话最容易被普通人用错的地方，不是太玄，而是会变成自责或甩锅的快捷键。遇到羞辱、操控、暴力、职场霸凌时，当然可以问自己为什么反应这么大，但不能因此推出“都是我的投射”。**内在反应是线索，不是判决；外部事实仍要被核对，边界仍要被保护。**更好的重构是三分法：这件事里有我的旧伤、对方的行为、以及关系中的互动模式。只认第一项会委屈自己，只认第二项会失去成长。
summaries.advice: 本周可做三步。第一，遇到强烈讨厌、嫉妒或羞耻，先写三列：我看到的事实、我脑中的解释、我被触发的旧感受。第二，借荣格的方法把指责换主语：“他太控制”改问“我何时也想控制？”但只当作自查，不当作替对方开脱。第三，借萨特的方法去问真人：“我理解的是……对吗？你怎么想？”**先分清事实、投射和边界，再决定靠近、沟通、道歉或离开。**
summaries.summary_en: The strongest shared lesson is that we never see other people as if through a neutral camera. Our feelings, language, bodily wiring, shame, and projections all help compose the image. **Other people often reveal something about us, but that does not make them merely ours.** The real disagreement is about the boundary. Some voices loosen the grip of self and other; Jung asks us to reclaim projection; neuroscience shows the boundary is flexible. Sartre and Wittgenstein pull the other way: another person has a freedom we cannot absorb, and the self is tested in public words and deeds.
summaries.insight_en: The sentence becomes dangerous when it turns into a shortcut for self-blame or evasion. If someone humiliates, manipulates, assaults, or bullies you, it may still be useful to ask why the reaction hits so hard—but that does not mean “it is all my projection.” **An inner reaction is a clue, not a verdict; external facts still have to be checked and boundaries still have to be protected.** A more practical frame has three parts: my old wound, the other person’s actual behavior, and the pattern between us. Seeing only the first can make you swallow harm; seeing only the second can block growth.
summaries.advice_en: Try three small practices this week. First, when someone triggers strong disgust, envy, anger, or shame, make three columns: observable facts, the story I am adding, and the old feeling being touched. Second, use Jung’s move carefully: change “he is controlling” into “where do I also try to control?”—as self-inquiry, not as an excuse for him. Third, use Sartre’s corrective: ask the real person, “Here is how I’m reading this; is that accurate? What do you mean?” **Separate fact, projection, and boundary before you choose to move closer, apologize, confront, or leave.**

summaries.summary: 这场圆桌并未在抹杀客观存在的肉体边界，全场的最大共识在于承认：**我们对『他人』的初始感知，总是无可避免地被自身的内部过滤网——无论是心理阴影、神经镜像还是语言习惯——所深度扭曲。** 六位思想家都同意，我们眼中的世界很大程度上是自我的回声。真正的分歧点在于如何处理这面『过滤网』：慧能和庄子主张消解人我边界以求精神的融通与自由；荣格和拉马钱德兰认为必须先看清并接纳自身的投射机制，才能在神经与心理层面真正理解他人；而萨特和维特根斯坦则极力反向拉扯，严厉警告我们不能沉溺于这种投射，必须去直面那个不受自我控制的、实打实的自由他者与外部世界。
summaries.insight: 现代数字生存让这句话发生了一种极其具象的物理变异。在算法推荐与社交网络中，你看到的『别人』，在数据层面上确实就是你自己。**系统通过精准追踪你的每一次点击与停留，为你生成了一个全是你自身偏见、恐惧与欲望的镜像世界，却将其伪装成丰富客观的『众生相』。** 萨特担忧我们因怯懦而把他人化约成自我内心的投影，但在今天，算法作为完美的中介，自动且高效地替我们完成了这种降维。我们不仅面临心理学上的『阴影投射』，更被困在技术层面的信息同质化牢笼里。如果我们不主动去触碰系统之外的真实摩擦，『你眼中的别人才是自己』就不再是一句充满哲理的自省，而将沦为一场盛大的数字自欺。
summaries.advice: 结合心理机制与现实环境，这里有两点本周即可上手的行动：**第一，执行一次『反向触碰』以打破数字与心理的镜像。** 本周刻意去阅读两篇与你既有立场完全相反的深度文章，或与一个你平时觉得『话不投机』的人展开十分钟的对话。全程闭嘴倾听，不反驳、不下定义，仅仅去感受『世界还有如此运转的逻辑』。第二，合并荣格的『阴影认领』与萨特的『提问法』。当某人激起你强烈的愤怒或鄙夷时，先在纸上写下『我是否在某些角落也恰恰如此？』；然后，去向对方抛出一个没有预设答案的开放式问题。用真实的惊奇，去击碎你脑补出的内心戏。
summaries.summary_en: The roundtable does not attempt to erase physical boundaries; rather, the greatest consensus across the board is acknowledging that **our initial perception of 'others' is always inevitably distorted by our internal filters—be it psychological shadows, neural mirroring, or linguistic habits.** All six thinkers agree that the world we see is largely an echo of the self. The true divergence lies in how to handle this 'filter.' Huineng and Zhuangzi advocate dissolving the boundaries between self and other to achieve spiritual freedom. Jung and Ramachandran argue that we must first recognize and accept our projection mechanisms to genuinely understand others. Conversely, Sartre and Wittgenstein forcefully push back, warning us not to indulge in these projections, urging us to face the uncontrollable, free 'Other' and the shared external world.
summaries.insight_en: Modern digital existence has given this philosophical quote a highly concrete, physical mutation. In the realm of algorithmic recommendations and social networks, the 'others' you see are, on a data level, quite literally yourself. **The system meticulously tracks every click and pause to construct a mirrored world made entirely of your own biases, fears, and desires, all disguised as an objective 'multitude of voices.'** Sartre worried that cowardice makes us reduce others to our own psychological projections; today, algorithms act as perfect intermediaries, automatically executing this reduction for us. We are not just facing psychological 'shadow projection' but are trapped in a technological cage of informational homogenization. If we do not actively seek out real friction outside the system, 'the others in your eyes are exactly yourself' ceases to be a philosophical introspection and becomes a grand digital self-deception.
summaries.advice_en: Combining psychological mechanisms with our current reality, here are two actionable steps for this week: **First, execute a 'reverse contact' to break your digital and psychological mirrors.** Deliberately read two in-depth articles that completely contradict your current stance, or have a ten-minute conversation with someone you usually find disagreeable. Listen without interrupting or defining them, just to experience that 'the world operates on this logic too.' Second, merge Jung's 'shadow reclamation' with Sartre's 'questioning method.' When someone triggers intense anger or contempt in you, first write down: 'Are there hidden corners where I act exactly like this?' Then, ask that person an open-ended question with no preset answer. Use genuine surprise to shatter the internal drama you’ve projected onto them.

hooks.text: **镜子，还是墙？**同一句『别人即自己』，能让你更使劲去看那个具体的人，也能替你免去看他的麻烦。区分真洞见与自我安慰的唯一试金石，或许是：它让你对别人更好奇，还是让好奇就此关门？该如何把它牢牢用成开门的那一种？
hooks.text_en: **A mirror, or a wall?** The same line — 'others are yourself' — can make you look harder at the actual person, or excuse you from looking at all. Perhaps the one test that separates real insight from self-comfort is this: does it deepen your curiosity about others, or shut it down? How do we keep it firmly the door-opening kind?

hooks.text: **当『这是你的投射』成了消音器。**心理学话术一旦反手用出去，就能让别人合理的批评不战自溃——『你只是太敏感』『你那是投射』。从自我觉察滑到人际操纵，谦卑就变成了煤气灯。一道清晰的界线该画在哪：什么时候『这是投射』是镜子，什么时候它只是盾牌？
hooks.text_en: **When 'that's your projection' becomes a mute button.** Turn psychology-talk outward and it can collapse another person's legitimate criticism without a fight — 'you're just too sensitive,' 'that's your projection.' Slide from self-awareness into manipulation and humility becomes gaslighting. Where should the clear line fall: when is 'that's projection' a mirror, and when is it merely a shield?

hooks.text: **你的投射，还是你的吗？**我们默认『看人的那双眼睛』属于自己，可今天你对一个陌生群体的第一印象，常被推荐流与算法预先调好。你以为投射出去的『别人』，有一大半是平台替你预装的。该向内审视的，便不止『我的阴影是什么』，还有『是谁在替我决定，我先看见别人哪一面』。
hooks.text_en: **Your projection — is it still yours?** We assume the eyes that judge others are our own, yet today your first impression of an unfamiliar group is often pre-tuned by a feed and an algorithm. The 'other' you think you project is, in large part, pre-installed by the platform. What needs inward scrutiny is not only 'what is my shadow' but 'who decides which side of others I see first?'

hooks.text: **共情是会萎缩的肌肉。**镜像神经元让你天生就能在自己身上重演别人，但这套硬件靠真实的同场相处来维持；长期只对着屏幕里的投影，模拟他人的能力会变钝。比起争论『别人是不是我』，更迫切的也许是：怎样的日常与城市设计，能让这块『理解他人的肌肉』不退化？
hooks.text_en: **Empathy is a muscle that can atrophy.** Mirror neurons let you re-enact others within yourself by birthright, but this hardware is maintained by real, in-person presence; live only among the projections on a screen and the capacity to simulate others dulls. More pressing than arguing 'is the other me' may be: what kind of daily life and urban design keep this 'muscle for understanding others' from wasting away?
